title: Race condition in interrupt handling
detail: The code doesn't properly handle race conditions where a KeyboardInterrupt might occur during the execution of the main loop, potentially causing unhandled tracebacks instead of proper abort handling.

title: Missing timeout in subprocess call
detail: The code uses subprocess.Popen without setting a timeout, which can cause the program to hang indefinitely if the subprocess doesn't respond. This is particularly problematic in interrupt scenarios where responsiveness is critical.

title: Missing error handling for sys.exit()
detail: The code calls sys.exit(exit_code) without any exception handling. If sys.exit() fails (e.g., due to a broken pipe or other I/O errors), the program will crash instead of gracefully handling the exit. This could lead to unhandled exceptions in environments where sys.exit() is not properly supported.

title: Potential NoneType error in _get_endmarker_and_dedents
detail: In the `_get_endmarker_and_dedents` function, line 691 assigns `current = current.parent` when `sibling is None`. If `current` has no parent (i.e., it's already at the root of the tree), this could lead to a NoneType error when trying to access `current.parent` in subsequent iterations. The code doesn't handle the case where `current` becomes None, which can happen if we traverse up to the root and there are no more parents.

title: Potential incorrect prefix handling in fmt off blocks
detail: In the main logic of `stringify_node`, when handling unclosed fmt: off blocks, the code assumes that all nodes in `eof_nodes` will have prefixes to be cleared. However, if there are no fmt: on directives found in the EOF nodes, it tries to join and clear prefixes from all eof_nodes without checking if they actually contain meaningful prefixes. This could lead to incorrect behavior when processing nodes that don't have trailing content.

title: Incorrect handling of non-ENDMARKER siblings
detail: In `_get_endmarker_and_dedents`, when a sibling is not a DEDENT or ENDMARKER, the code assumes it's a Leaf and returns it along with dedents. However, if the sibling is not an ENDMARKER but also not a DEDENT, this could lead to incorrect behavior because the function expects to only encounter DEDENTs or ENDMARKER when traversing backwards from a node to ENDMARKER. The logic should ensure that we're properly handling all possible sibling types.

title: Incorrect conditional logic in stop method
detail: The fix introduces a logical error in the condition checking. The original code only printed a blank line for non-interactive consoles when progress was not disabled. The new code prints a blank line if the console is NOT interactive OR is Jupyter, but only when progress is not disabled. This creates inconsistency - it should only print when the console is non-interactive AND progress is enabled, or when progress is disabled and no output should occur.

title: Incorrect lock acquisition logic
detail: The code incorrectly checks `self._export_lock.locked` which is a method, not a property. This will always return True (since it's a callable), causing the code to always go to the else branch and call `maybe_deferred_to_future(self._export_lock.acquire())` even when the lock is free. This creates a race condition where multiple concurrent calls can cause deadlocks or incorrect behavior in the feed export locking mechanism.

title: Incorrect scalar type checking
detail: The code checks `type(value) in _SCALAR_TYPES` but this will not work correctly for subclasses. For example, if a custom class inherits from int, `type(value)` will be the subclass type, not int, so it won't match. This means that scalar values like custom integer subclasses won't be properly optimized and will go through the normal serialization path.

title: Inverted logic in accept_html
detail: The logic was inverted from the previous implementation. Previously, 'accept_html' returned True if 'text/html' was in the accept header or if 'accept_xhtml' was True. Now it returns True only if 'text/html' is NOT in self, which breaks the intended behavior of matching HTML content types.

title: Missing import for warnings module
detail: The code uses 'warnings.warn' but doesn't import the warnings module at the top of the file. This will cause a NameError when the deprecated property is accessed.
